correctness.rationale: The Poisson expansion is exact as a bounded operator on BV inputs; conditional products of uniforms give an explicit compound-Poisson gamma mixture. Every signed BV measure is a superposition of upper-interval jumps, and the nonnegative one-jump defect bounds the integral norm. Its derivative is exactly the truncated exponential moment minus one, equal to \(e^{-t}I_0(2\sqrt{t\log(1/s)})-1\), which strictly decreases in \(s\) and has one root. The optimizer is attained by and only by a single jump there. The Bessel root expansion gives the short- and long-time locations; a two-region dominated-convergence bound proves the sharp large-time deficit prefactor. Independent implementation of finite Poisson and Bessel integrals passed 108 numeric comparisons; none are used as proof of the infinite-time result.

value.rationale: This is a natural exact BV approximation problem for the positive continuous-time semigroup generated by the classical Hardy average. The sharp Bessel-defined step and the \(t/4+(\log t)/4\) location law yield quantitative information not encoded in any fixed iterate or conventional spectral norm, and the \(2(2\pi t)^{-1/4}e^{-t/4}\) deficit calibrates the least accurate discontinuous input. The parameter is semigroup time, not an arbitrary finite slice.
